chunks: Sa'd, from Abū Ja'far, from al-Ḥusayn, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Ismā'īl ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

I asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام about wearing leather garments, khuffs, and sandals, and performing salat (prayer) in them when they were not from the land of the Muslims. He said: “As for the sandals and the khuffs, there is no harm in them.”

key_terms.الْجُلُودِ: leather items or skins used as clothing
key_terms.الْخِفَافِ: khuffs; leather footwear covering the feet
key_terms.الْمُصَلِّينَ: the Muslims, literally those who perform salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in sandals and khuffs from non-Muslim lands according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a jurisprudential ruling concerning salat (prayer) in footwear and leather items obtained from non-Muslim lands. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem with praying in sandals and khuffs in such a case.
